executive_summary: Bottom line: the week's biggest moves were about controlling and measuring AI agents, not building them. Halden and Orbitco published an open standard for how agents log in to businesses, and Brightpath launched a tool that ties workflow changes to business KPIs, which is the job Quillon Agents sells.

company_summaries.title: Agent identity standards led by Halden
company_summaries.what_matters: Halden and Orbitco announced the Open Agent Protocol on Oct 6 with Greenmart, Marketloft, Payrill and Kestrel Voice as partners; a v0.1 specification is due later in October,
company_summaries.why: so agent identity is becoming a buying question in Quillon Agents deals.

company_summaries.title: Brightpath bundles AI ROI measurement
company_summaries.what_matters: Brightpath made AI Workflow Factory generally available on Oct 6; it finds workflow improvements with process mining and measures them against KPIs such as case deflection,
company_summaries.why: which overlaps with Quillon Agents' ROI story for any customer already on Brightpath.

company_summaries.title: Corvane's 2,000-person AI value team
company_summaries.what_matters: Corvane launched an Advanced Intelligence Group of more than 2,000 AI specialists on Oct 5, aimed at clients that have not turned AI pilots into lasting value,
company_summaries.why: which is the same buyer Quillon's consulting work targets.

company_summaries.title: Legal tech consolidation
company_summaries.what_matters: All six tracked Quillon Legal competitors were quiet; the legal market's news came from acquisitions and a $17m raise by the AI-native law firm Larkin Law,

company_summaries.title: Low-cost certificates raise the baseline

updates.what: On Oct 6, 2026 Halden and Orbitco announced the Open Agent Protocol, an open standard that lets a consumer's personal AI agent sign in to a business and be limited to the actions that business allows. It uses OpenAuth, the same login handshake behind 'Sign in with Searchly', and lets a business choose guest or signed-in access and whether the agent works through its website, its APIs or its own agent. Launch partners are Kestrel Voice, Tallow, Orbitco, Vantor, Marketloft, Payrill and Greenmart. A v0.1 specification is due later in October, and payments are left out of the first release.
facts: Partners: Kestrel Voice, Tallow, Vantor, Marketloft, Payrill, Greenmart
v0.1 specification due later in October 2026
Payments excluded from the first release
Marketloft and Payrill also joined Ledgerline's competing Verified Agent Protocol
updates.why: Halden is now setting the rules for how agents prove who they are and what they may do, not only selling agents. Enterprise buyers in Quillon Agents deals will start asking how we record which agent did what, and Quillon clients building customer-facing agents will ask whether to support this standard.
updates.response: Add agent identity and permission records to the Quillon Agents roadmap discussion and track the v0.1 specification when it ships.

updates.what: On Oct 6, 2026, at its World Forum in Mumbai, Brightpath (which owns Fieldwise) made AI Workflow Factory generally available. The product combines process mining, which reads system logs to see how work really flows, with an autonomous engineering agent that builds the fix inside Brightpath. Each improvement is tied to a KPI the business already tracks; Brightpath's example is raising case deflection by 20% across several business units at once. Brightpath says it runs more than 100 billion workflows a year, and the Autonomous Engineer part is in early access on request.
facts: Ties each change to an existing business KPI (example: +20% case deflection)
Autonomous Engineer in early access on request
Brightpath's own figure: 100 billion+ workflows a year
updates.why: Measuring the business impact of AI changes is the core of Quillon Agents' pitch, and Brightpath now bundles a version of it for its own customers. In accounts that already run Brightpath, buyers will ask why they need a separate ROI layer.
updates.response: Write a one-page comparison showing Quillon Agents measures AI ROI across every vendor's tools, not only work done inside Brightpath.

updates.what: On Oct 5, 2026 Corvane launched its Advanced Intelligence Group, a global network of more than 2,000 specialists in AI, data, industries and technology platforms, led by Chief AI and Data Officer Dr. Mara Quill. The group focuses on agentic AI, advanced data work, supply chain and engineering, and Datavault and Icefield platforms. Corvane names two client projects: AI demand forecasting at Medlink and wallet infrastructure with Nordcom Global. Its stated reason is its own research finding that only about a quarter of C-suite leaders see widespread, lasting value from AI.
facts: 2,000+ specialists, led by Dr. Mara Quill
Focus: agentic AI, data, supply chain, Datavault and Icefield
Corvane's own claim: about a quarter of C-suite leaders see lasting AI value
updates.why: Corvane is packaging a dedicated team for exactly the 'pilots that never paid off' problem Quillon sells against. Large enterprise buyers now have a branded Corvane option, so Quillon needs a sharper answer on speed, senior engineers and handover to win mid-market work.
updates.response: Update Quillon's pitch to contrast a small senior team that hands the system over with a 2,000-person group.

updates.what: On Oct 5, 2026 Learnwell announced that its Data Engineering Professional Certificate is now available on its own learning platform. It is a multi-course certificate for data engineering skills, not an agent-building or the Quillon model course. No new agentic AI course from Learnwell appeared in the window. The release continues its pattern of low-cost certificates sold directly to individual learners.
facts: Data Engineering Professional Certificate, on Learnwell's own platform
No new agentic AI or the Quillon model course in the window
updates.why: The launch is outside our topic, so it does not compete directly with Quillon Academy cohorts. It does show Learnwell moving certificates onto its own platform, which keeps raising the free and low-cost baseline our paid cohorts are compared with.
updates.response: Keep positioning Learnwell courses as optional prework, not a substitute.

new_entrants.name: Marlow PROOF and Gateway
new_entrants.note: Marlow, a customer-service agent company, introduced a permission protocol that verifies an agent's identity and authorisations with audit trails, plus a gateway that detects AI agents arriving at a company's systems (Oct 6-7). It sits next to Halden's standard and overlaps with Quillon Agents' agent-governance story.

new_entrants.name: Terra by Aeon Labs
new_entrants.note: Aeon Labs's founders launched Terra on Oct 5, a testing platform that builds synthetic companies with 66 product simulators so teams can test AI agents without real production data. It is relevant to how Quillon proves agents work before handover.

new_entrants.name: Larkin Law
new_entrants.note: A new-model, AI-heavy law firm, Larkin Law raised $17m (Oct 1). Firms like this buy contract tools directly and are a possible Quillon Legal customer type as well as a sign of where legal work is moving.

new_entrants.name: Legal acquisitions
new_entrants.note: Folio 2 bought Casebinder (Oct 1) and Brief.io bought Open Brief (Sep 30), continuing the consolidation of legal tech vendors around Quillon Legal's market.

working_well.title: Shipping a standard with big partners
working_well.body: Halden launched its protocol with Orbitco, Greenmart, Marketloft and Payrill on day one, which gives a young standard instant credibility with enterprise buyers.

working_well.title: Tying AI changes to KPIs the customer already tracks
working_well.body: Brightpath sells AI Workflow Factory on a concrete outcome, such as 20% more case deflection, rather than on model features, which is easier for a buyer to approve.

working_well.title: Naming the value gap in the launch
working_well.body: Corvane opened its new group with its own statistic that only about a quarter of C-suite leaders see lasting AI value, turning a market problem into a reason to hire it.

market_trends.body: Agent identity and permissions became a product category this week: Halden with Orbitco, Marlow's PROOF and Ledgerline's Verified Agent Protocol all compete to define how agents prove who they are.

Measuring AI outcomes is moving into the big platforms: Brightpath ties workflow changes to KPIs and Corvane sells a team for the AI value gap, so standalone ROI tools must prove neutrality across vendors.

threats.title: Brightpath bundles AI ROI measurement
threats.why: AI Workflow Factory gives Brightpath customers KPI-linked AI measurement inside a platform they already pay for.
threats.impact: Longer sales cycles and price pressure for Quillon Agents in accounts that run on Brightpath.

threats.title: Agent identity standards led by Halden
threats.why: If buyers adopt Halden's protocol, they will expect every agent tool to record agent identity and permissions.
threats.impact: Quillon Agents may be asked for agent audit features it does not yet show in demos.

threats.title: Legal tech consolidation
threats.why: Acquisitions by Brief.io and Folio 2 build bundled suites that can include contract review at little extra cost.
threats.impact: Smaller law firms and in-house teams may choose a bundle over a specialist contract tool like Quillon Legal.

threats.title: Corvane's 2,000-person AI value team
threats.why: Corvane now offers a branded team aimed at the same stalled-pilot problem Quillon solves.
threats.impact: Harder to win large enterprise consulting work against Corvane's scale and existing relationships.

threats.title: Low-cost certificates raise the baseline
threats.why: Learnwell keeps adding inexpensive certificates on its own platform, which shapes what learners expect to pay.
threats.impact: More price objections to $3,000 cohorts from individual learners.

opportunities.title: Be the vendor-neutral ROI layer
opportunities.body: Brightpath measures only work done in Brightpath, so Quillon Agents can sell measurement across Brightpath, Assistly, the Quillon model and other agents in one view.

opportunities.title: Sell to AI-native law firms
opportunities.body: Funded firms like Larkin Law need contract review tools quickly and have no legacy contract system, which suits Quillon Legal's playbook-based review.

opportunities.title: Win the mid-market Corvane will not staff
opportunities.body: Corvane's new group targets large clients like Medlink, leaving mid-market legal and finance teams open for Quillon's smaller, senior teams with handover built in.

opportunities.title: Teach agent identity and governance
opportunities.body: The new agent identity protocols give the Quillon Academy a timely module on agent permissions and audit that general AI PM courses do not cover yet.
